trust_decision.summary: Untrusted bundler module ids are turned into output filenames by single-pass string replace, so `....//node_modules/...` becomes `../node_modules/...` and the CLI joins it onto the output dir and writes it outside `-o`; the conversion decision lives in per-backend sanitizers in crates/core and the containment decision at the CLI join/write.

landing_point.why: The only place that converts a module filename into a filesystem path: `deduplicate_path(&out_dir.join(filename), ...)`, followed by `create_dir_all(parent)` and `fs::write` at crates/cli/src/main.rs:249-259. A reader of 'arbitrary file write during unpack' looks here first and sees no containment check at all.

fix_sites.entry_point: `wakaru_core::unpack_bundle` / `try_unpack_bundle` public API (the fix adds the shared component-based helper beside it)
`wakaru_core::unpack` on an esbuild bundle (reached by CLI --unpack)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The four per-backend sanitizers are internal string helpers in another crate, and sanitizing the joined path once at the CLI write is enough for every backend, so changing the producers (and the library/wasm API they feed) looks redundant; separately, `--extract` looks covered because its own resolver already drops `..`/root components.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A module id that only looks like traversal is legitimate and must still unpack: `....//node_modules/@wakaru/cli/bin/wakaru` has to be written as `<out>/..../node_modules/...`, and traversal components are expected to be dropped rather than reject the bundle (`../../../etc/passwd` -> `etc/passwd`). An over-broad `contains("..")` / `replace("..","")` gate breaks the first, and the repo's own helper already encodes the opposite convention (`!name.contains("..")`), which invites exactly that over-broad fix.

O6_input_shapes: overlapping-dot ids a single replace pass turns into `../` (`....//node_modules/@wakaru/cli/bin/wakaru`)
empty or traversal-only ids (`../../..`, `..\..\`, `./`) falling back to `unknown.js` / `unknown` / `module.js`
a pre-existing symlinked parent directory inside the output dir (`link/pwn.js`)
a regular file where a parent directory is expected (`src/index.js` with `src` a file)
duplicate filenames needing `index_2.js` de-duplication after the safety checks

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `wakaru extract <map> -o DIR` writes every source-map `sources` entry under DIR with only lexical sanitation: a source entry `link/pwn.js` with a pre-existing `<DIR>/link` directory symlink writes outside DIR (the output dir is also never canonicalized), which is exactly what the published fix's unpack path now rejects.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: `--extract` is a separate source-map command, not bundle unpack, and its path builder `resolve_source_path` already drops `..`, root and drive-prefix components, so it looks protected.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same CLI file, different command; its resolver sits in another crate file (crates/core/src/sourcemap_rename.rs:64-88)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared `write_output_file(out_dir, relative, content)` used by both `--unpack` and `--extract`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both commands already write attacker-named relative paths under the same `-o` directory, so a maintainer refactoring the fix would naturally route extract through the new helpers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a final `ensure_inside(out_dir, filename)` applied in `assign_unique_module_filenames` for multi-input unpack
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: multi-file unpack already owns filename de-duplication there, so a defence-in-depth containment check that assumes nothing about the backends belongs at that point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a `saveAll`/zip export in the wasm binding (or playground) that writes `WakaruModule.filename` as a path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the binding already hands module filenames straight to JS and the playground already displays them, so a download/zip-of-modules feature would write them with no validation.

O9_family: path traversal / improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory (CWE-22) in unpack output paths

O10_build.toolchain: cargo workspace (crates/core, crates/cli, crates/wasm), edition 2021, stable rustc; swc_core 65, rayon, sourcemap, similar, insta (dev), clap
O10_build.project_tests: Inline unit tests in crates/cli/src/main.rs `mod tests` (temp-dir CLI runs) and per unpacker (webpack5.rs:1469-1498, webpack4.rs:1883-1893, systemjs.rs:900-935); integration tests crates/core/tests/webpack_fixtures.rs (incl. wp_path_traversal_sanitized at :342-347 and assert_no_traversal at :43-50), bundle_unpack.rs, webpack4_unpack*.rs, esbuild_unpack.rs, systemjs_unpack.rs, webpack5_chunk_unpack.rs, multi_file_unpack.rs; fixtures committed under crates/core/tests/bundles and insta snapshots under crates/core/tests/snapshots.

j.j_sites_touched: crates/cli/src/main.rs; crates/core/src/unpacker/mod.rs; crates/core/src/unpacker/esbuild.rs; crates/core/src/unpacker/systemjs.rs; crates/core/src/unpacker/webpack4.rs; crates/core/src/unpacker/webpack5.rs
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a `filename.contains("..")` rejection (or `replace("..","")`) at the CLI join, or only rewrite webpack5::sanitize_filename from the reproduced bundle: that leaves the sibling backends, absolute/backslash shapes and the library API unfixed, and as a rejection it also breaks legitimate `....`-named modules that must still be written under the output dir.

out_of_scope_notes: The wasm binding (crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:66-100) forwards unpack filenames to JS and the in-repo playground only displays them, so no write route beyond the CLI sink was pursued; npm/bin/wakaru merely spawns the platform binary.
